title: Coagulation results: DIC, liver disease and anticoagulants

header.contentArea: Applied surgical science and critical care

BSH platelet transfusion guideline (2017; review date January 2022)

brief.scenario: Mr Stanley Cobb, 64, is on day 3 after an emergency laparotomy and Hartmann's procedure for faecal peritonitis. He is on prophylactic enoxaparin. This evening he is oozing from his wound, drain site and cannula sites. His coagulation results have just come back.
brief.task: The examiner will show you his results, then results from two other patients. Interpret them and explain your management.

beforeYouWalkIn.frame: Read every result against its range, name the pattern, score it, treat the cause, then products for bleeding only.
beforeYouWalkIn.trap: Transfusing to fix numbers while the septic source goes untreated, or giving the next enoxaparin dose.
beforeYouWalkIn.firstMove: "I'll read each result against its range and his preoperative values."

grid.label: Systematic read
grid.fail: Picks out one abnormal value and stops.
grid.pass: Reads each result against its range: haemoglobin, platelets, PT, APTT, fibrinogen, D-dimer; asks about his drugs.
grid.high: Compares with preoperative values (platelets were 260) and asks for repeat tests to follow the trend.

grid.label: Recognising and scoring DIC
grid.fail: Calls it liver disease or heparin, or can't name a pattern.
grid.pass: Falling platelets, long PT and APTT, low fibrinogen, very high D-dimer in sepsis: DIC. ISTH (2001) score 7; 5 or more is overt DIC.
grid.high: Scores it aloud: platelets 42 = 2, PT 7.5 s long = 2, strong D-dimer rise = 3, fibrinogen 1.2 = 0.

grid.label: Treating the cause (safety-critical)
grid.fail: Transfuses and waits; doesn't see him or look for sepsis.
grid.pass: Sees him now; NEWS2 8 with suspected abdominal sepsis: IV antibiotics within 1 hour; 250 ml crystalloid boluses, reassessing each.
grid.high: Senior advice if no better after 1,000 ml; source control with the consultant, as products only buy time.

grid.label: Plasma and cryoprecipitate
grid.fail: Gives nothing while he bleeds, or transfuses without rechecking.
grid.pass: Clinically significant bleeding with PT and APTT ratios above 1.5: consider FFP. Fibrinogen 1.2, below 1.5: consider cryoprecipitate, 2 pools.
grid.high: Rechecks clotting and fibrinogen after each and gives more if needed; wouldn't give either if he weren't bleeding.

grid.label: Platelets
grid.fail: Ignores a platelet count of 42 in a bleeding patient, or transfuses a non-bleeding patient on numbers alone.
grid.pass: Bleeding DIC after surgery, platelets under 50: considers platelet transfusion (BSH DIC guideline), deciding with haematology.
grid.high: Knows NICE and BSH thresholds differ and depend on bleeding severity; wouldn't transfuse on the count alone or once bleeding stops.

grid.label: Heparin and tranexamic acid (safety-critical)
grid.fail: Gives tonight's enoxaparin, or tranexamic acid, without thinking.
grid.pass: Withholds prophylactic enoxaparin while he bleeds; keeps mechanical prophylaxis; reassesses VTE and bleeding risk.
grid.high: Restarts prophylaxis once bleeding stops, as DIC also clots; avoids antifibrinolytics unless haematology advises.

grid.label: DIC or liver disease?
grid.fail: Calls Mrs Ellery's results DIC and orders plasma.
grid.pass: Known cirrhosis, raised bilirubin, low albumin: coagulopathy of liver disease; the clinical context decides.
grid.high: Knows factor VIII and the ISTH score don't reliably separate DIC from liver disease.

grid.label: Warfarin: pattern and reversal
grid.fail: Gives FFP, or waits for vitamin K alone.
grid.pass: Isolated high INR on warfarin with severe bleeding: stops warfarin; immediate prothrombin complex concentrate and IV vitamin K.
grid.high: No FFP to reverse warfarin (NICE); checks the INR confirms reversal and considers more PCC.

failures.move: Transfusing products and leaving the septic source untreated.
failures.consequence: Safety-critical: the DIC continues while the cause is ignored.

failures.move: Giving the next enoxaparin dose, or tranexamic acid, to a bleeding patient with DIC.
failures.consequence: Safety-critical: more bleeding; BSH advises against antifibrinolytics in DIC in general.

failures.move: Giving FFP to reverse warfarin in a major bleed.
failures.consequence: Slower, incomplete reversal; NICE advises PCC instead.

failures.move: Giving plasma to a non-bleeding patient with cirrhosis to correct the PT.
failures.consequence: Exposes her to transfusion risks with no benefit.

recovery.line: Platelets, PT prolongation, D-dimer and fibrinogen; 5 or more is overt DIC.
The cornerstone is treating the cause: his abdominal sepsis.

knowledge.fact: ISTH 2001 overt DIC: platelets under 50 = 2, 50–99 = 1; D-dimer strong rise = 3, moderate = 2; PT 6 s or more long = 2, 3–6 s = 1; fibrinogen under 1 g/L = 1. Total 5 or more.
ISTH 2025: D-dimer over 3× and over 7× the upper limit score 2 and 3; his (about 17×) still scores 3.
BSH DIC (2009): products for bleeding, not numbers; platelets considered under 50 if bleeding or postoperative; cryoprecipitate if fibrinogen stays under 1 g/L despite FFP.
NICE NG24: platelets if clinically significant bleeding and under 30, up to 100 if severe or critical-site; cryoprecipitate if bleeding and fibrinogen under 1.5 g/L.
BSH platelets (2017): bleeding thresholds 30 (WHO grade 2), 50 (severe), 100 (trauma, brain, eye); a guide in DIC.
Abdominal surgery: stockings or intermittent pneumatic compression; reassess when the condition changes.
PCC corrects warfarin in about 30 minutes; vitamin K takes 4–6 hours.
Life-threatening bleeding on warfarin: stop it; phytomenadione 5–10 mg by slow IV injection with PCC.

recall.say: "This is DIC from abdominal sepsis: ISTH score 7. Treat the cause."
do: Products for bleeding only; hold enoxaparin

numbers.meaning: PT/APTT ratio for FFP; fibrinogen g/L for cryo, if bleeding
platelets: consider transfusion in bleeding DIC (BSH)

recall.trap: Correcting the numbers while the septic source goes unchecked.
recall.finish: Source control, targeted products, and prophylaxis restarted when bleeding stops.

sources.name: Levi M, Toh CH, Thachil J, Watson HG. Guidelines for the diagnosis and management of disseminated intravascular coagulation. British Committee for Standards in Haematology. Br J Haematol 2009;145:24-33 (BSH guideline summary)
sources.version: Published 13 February 2009; last review date 9 January 2012
sources.supports: Diagnosis uses clinical and laboratory information; the ISTH scoring system gives an objective measure; repeat the tests to follow the changing picture; treating the underlying condition is the cornerstone; platelets and plasma not given for laboratory results alone, generally only with bleeding; with bleeding or high bleeding risk (for example postoperative) and platelets under 50, consider platelet transfusion; FFP may help in bleeding patients with prolonged PT and APTT; severe hypofibrinogenaemia under 1 g/L persisting despite FFP may be treated with fibrinogen concentrate or cryoprecipitate; in critically ill, non-bleeding patients with DIC, prophylactic heparin or LMWH is recommended; in general, no antifibrinolytics in DIC

sources.name: Thachil J, Iba T. Designing the diagnostic criteria for disseminated intravascular coagulation (DIC). Juntendo Med J 2023;69(6):463-465, table 1 (ISTH overt DIC score of Taylor FB Jr et al, Thromb Haemost 2001;86:1327-30)
sources.supports: ISTH overt DIC score: platelets under 50 = 2, 50 to under 100 = 1; fibrin marker (D-dimer) strong increase = 3, moderate increase = 2; PT prolonged 6 s or more = 2, 3 to under 6 s = 1; fibrinogen under 1 g/L = 1; total 5 or more = overt DIC

sources.name: Iba T, Maier CL, Scarlatescu E, Levy JH. Introducing the new definition and diagnostic criteria of disseminated intravascular coagulation released by the International Society on Thrombosis and Haemostasis in 2025. Semin Thromb Hemost 2026;52(1):10-17
sources.supports: ISTH 2025 update: phase-based classification (pre-DIC, early-phase, overt); the overt DIC score is refined, with D-dimer above 3 and above 7 times the upper limit of normal scoring 2 and 3 points; platelet count, PT-INR and fibrinogen remain key indicators

sources.name: Estcourt LJ, Birchall J, Allard S, et al. Guidelines for the use of platelet transfusions (British Committee for Standards in Haematology). Br J Haematol 2017;176:365-394, with BSH summary (appendix 1)
sources.version: Published online 23 December 2016; last review date 14 January 2022
sources.supports: Therapeutic use (bleeding WHO grade 2 or above): bleeding not severe 30, severe bleeding 50, multiple trauma, brain or eye injury or spontaneous intracerebral haemorrhage 100 (x10^9/L); DIC: use the preprocedure or therapeutic thresholds as a guide with individual case review; prophylactic transfusion not indicated for platelet consumption such as DIC; in severe bleeding replace fibrinogen if below 1.5 g/L

sources.name: NICE NG24: Blood transfusion
sources.supports: Platelets: offer with clinically significant bleeding and count under 30; up to 100 for severe bleeding or critical sites (1.7.1-1.7.2); FFP: only consider with clinically significant bleeding and abnormal coagulation, for example PT or APTT ratio above 1.5 (1.9.1); do not offer FFP to correct abnormal coagulation in people who are not bleeding (unless a procedure with a risk of significant bleeding) or to reverse a vitamin K antagonist (1.9.2); reassess and repeat coagulation tests after FFP (1.10.1); cryoprecipitate: consider with clinically significant bleeding and fibrinogen under 1.5 g/L (1.11.1); adult dose 2 pools (1.12.1); repeat fibrinogen and give more if needed (1.12.2); immediate prothrombin complex concentrate for emergency warfarin reversal in severe bleeding (1.12.3); monitor the INR and consider further PCC (1.12.6)

sources.name: NICE NG89: Venous thromboembolism in over 16s: reducing the risk of hospital-acquired deep vein thrombosis or pulmonary embolism
sources.supports: Reassess VTE and bleeding risk when the clinical condition changes (1.1.8); abdominal surgery: mechanical prophylaxis with anti-embolism stockings or intermittent pneumatic compression (1.14.2); add pharmacological prophylaxis when VTE risk outweighs bleeding risk (1.14.3)

sources.name: NICE NG253: Suspected sepsis in people aged 16 or over: recognition, assessment and early management
sources.supports: High risk = NEWS2 7 or more; IV antibiotics within 1 hour (1.8.3); 250 ml crystalloid boluses up to 1,000 ml in total (1.8.6-1.8.7); senior advice if not improved after 1,000 ml (1.8.9); early surgical team for source control (1.11.4)

sources.name: Royal College of Physicians: National Early Warning Score (NEWS) 2, chart 1: the NEWS scoring system
sources.supports: NEWS2 parameter bands and aggregate score

sources.name: Allen C, Heskel M, Butt A, et al. Factor VIII levels and ISTH disseminated intravascular coagulation scores do not distinguish disseminated intravascular coagulation from the coagulopathy of liver disease. Acta Haematol 2025;148(2):220-225
sources.supports: In 123 patients with DIC, liver disease or both, factor VIII levels did not differ significantly; ISTH DIC scores are not predictive of DIC in liver disease

sources.name: Beriplex P/N 1000 IU (human prothrombin complex): Summary of Product Characteristics (emc 3031)
sources.supports: Correction of vitamin K antagonist-induced impairment is commonly reached about 30 minutes after injection; consider simultaneous vitamin K, which usually takes effect within 4-6 hours

sources.name: Konakion MM 10 mg/ml solution for injection (phytomenadione): Summary of Product Characteristics (emc 9755)
sources.supports: Severe or life-threatening haemorrhage during coumarin anticoagulant therapy: withdraw the coumarin and give phytomenadione 5-10 mg by slow intravenous injection (over at least 30 seconds) together with prothrombin complex concentrate (4.2)

sources.name: ICBSE Guide to the intercollegiate MRCS examination

partner.opening: Mr Cobb's coagulation results have just come back. Please interpret them.

reveals.finding: Hb 92 g/L (118 before surgery); platelets 42 ×10⁹/L (260); PT 19.5 s (range 10.5–13.5, control 12.0); APTT 52 s (range 25–35, ratio 1.7); fibrinogen 1.2 g/L (range 1.5–4.0); D-dimer 8,400 ng/ml FEU (under 500): the lab reports a strong increase.
Enoxaparin 40 mg daily, next dose due at 18:00. No antiplatelets or anticoagulants.

reveals.trigger: Asks for observations or sees him
reveals.finding: Temperature 38.6°C, pulse 118, BP 96/58, RR 24, SpO2 95% on air, alert: NEWS2 8. Abdomen distended and diffusely tender; turbid fluid in the drain.
Say: "Mrs Maureen Ellery, 58, has alcohol-related cirrhosis and is not bleeding." PT 17.0 s, APTT 38 s, platelets 78, fibrinogen 1.6 g/L, D-dimer 900 (under 500), bilirubin 44, albumin 27.
Say: "Mr Victor Quayle, 79, takes warfarin for AF. He has melaena, BP 88/50. INR 7.8; platelets and APTT normal."

push.question: Calculate his ISTH DIC score.
push.expect: Platelets 42 = 2, PT 7.5 s long = 2, strong D-dimer = 3, fibrinogen 1.2 = 0: 7, overt DIC.

push.question: What will you give him, and why?
push.expect: He is bleeding: FFP for ratios above 1.5, cryoprecipitate 2 pools for fibrinogen under 1.5; consider platelets under 50 (BSH DIC; NICE uses 30 for this grade); recheck after each.

push.question: What about his enoxaparin?
push.expect: Hold while bleeding, mechanical prophylaxis, restart when bleeding stops.

curveballs.prompt: The F1 asks to give Mrs Ellery plasma before tomorrow's ward round because her PT is long.
curveballs.safeAnswer: No: she isn't bleeding and no procedure is planned; NICE advises against FFP to correct numbers.

curveballs.prompt: The ward sister suggests tranexamic acid for Mr Cobb's oozing.
curveballs.safeAnswer: BSH advises against antifibrinolytics in DIC generally; only on haematology advice.

curveballs.prompt: After FFP and cryoprecipitate his fibrinogen is 0.8 and he's still bleeding.
curveballs.safeAnswer: More cryoprecipitate or fibrinogen concentrate with haematology, recheck, and push for source control.
